index.html.title: API overview | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
index.html.summary: 2D Tower Defense Maker API The reference documents the public and protected API of the three product assemblies. The TDMaker.* namespaces and assembly names are the identifiers used in your Unity project. Start with the user manual for installation, editor workflows and playable samples. Select the product logo above to return to the manual. Use this reference when writing integrations, building content from code or extending the simulation. Assembly Responsibility Start here TDMaker.Core Engine-independent simulation, immutable definitions, player commands, entities and events Simulation, definitions, commands TDMaker.Unity ScriptableObject authoring, scene integration, views, HUD, localization and campaign progress LevelAsset, SimulationRunner, authoring namespace TDMaker.Editor Level creation, validation, authoring windows and simulation previews Editor namespace, ProjectValidator, LevelDryRun Working with the simulation Bake a LevelAsset into immutable definitions, create a Simulation, enqueue player commands and advance fixed ticks with Step(). Consume simulation events before clearing them. SimulationRunner performs this integration for a Unity scene and exposes the current simulation for custom controls. TDMaker.Core has no Unity engine dependency. Keep gameplay rules in the simulation and use TDMaker.Unity to present state and translate user input into commands. Editor APIs belong in editor-only assemblies. Reference scope This reference is generated from the product's actual C# declarations and XML documentation using DocFX 2.81.0 with local Unity 6000.4.1f1 references. It includes exported types and members, overloads, parameters, return values and available examples. Private implementation, product source files and source links are excluded from the published site. The documentation generator runs separately from the site build. A site build reads the checked-in API metadata and does not require Unity, the product source code or the local compiled assemblies.

reference/TDMaker.Core.CommandFailure.ht.title: Enum CommandFailure | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Core.CommandFailure.ht.summary: Enum CommandFailure Namespace TDMaker.Core Assembly TDMaker.Core.dll Machine-readable command failure reasons. public enum CommandFailure Fields CapacityExceeded = 19 A required fixed pool or input queue is full. GameEnded = 1 The game has a terminal outcome. InsufficientGold = 6 The purchase cannot be funded or its investment ledger would overflow. InsufficientPoints = 15 The required hero level or free point budget is missing. InvalidAbility = 13 The ability or skill slot does not exist. InvalidCommand = 12 The command type is not supported. InvalidEntity = 7 The required entity or component does not exist. InvalidPoint = 16 The shared placement policy rejected the point. InvalidRallyPoint = 9 The point is invalid or no lane placement exists within the rally radius. InvalidSlot = 2 The build slot index is outside the level. InvalidUpgrade = 8 The destination is not an immediate upgrade target. None = 0 No failure applies. NotImplemented = 11 The command is reserved for a later milestone. RankLimit = 14 The ability or skill has reached its rank cap. SlotOccupied = 3 The build slot is already reserved. SpellUnavailable = 18 The spell is locked, cooling, or already cast this tick. UnavailableTower = 5 The tower is not available for construction in this level. UnknownSpell = 17 The spell slot has no authored definition. UnknownTemplate = 4 The requested tower template does not exist. WaveUnavailable = 10 The next wave cannot currently be called.

reference/TDMaker.Core.html.title: Namespace TDMaker.Core | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Core.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Core Classes BeamBinding Pooled channel state, valid only while present in Simulation.Beams. CommandLog Fixed-capacity input recording with seed and versioned binary persistence. Record only external Enqueue calls between ticks. CompanionSlot One preallocated owner slot, including its pending insertion. CustomDataSlots Type-keyed runtime slots, allocated once per entity during extension registration. Entity A pooled runtime entity. Keep its Id, not its reference, across removals. EntityStore Deferred entity storage with stable iteration order and prewarmed component bundles. GameState Read-only public economy, wave, and outcome state. RemainsRecord A pooled neutral body record. Retain Id, rather than the object, after it leaves Simulation.Remains. SimConfig Immutable fixed-step and preallocation settings. SimLimits Fixed M2 pool sizes. Saturated requests fail without allocating in the tick path. SimRandom A reproducible xorshift32 random stream; zero seeds are remapped. Simulation A deterministic fixed-step world. Use commands for player actions and ClearEvents after reading output. SimulationClock A bounded frame accumulator implementing the product catch-up policy without engine dependencies. SpatialQueryBuffer Caller-owned fixed-capacity query storage. Entries are valid until this buffer is queried again. TrapBinding Pooled deployment state, valid only while present in Simulation.Traps; retain Id across removals. UpgradeShopRules Storage-independent immutable star-shop transitions. Forced battle ranks never affect spending. Structs CommandRecord An immutable command and the fixed tick at which it was submitted for processing. DamageContext A modifiable raw damage request, before defense and incoming multipliers. DamageResult One accepted request after resolution; ignored, removed, or immune recipients produce zero damage. EarlyCallRewardPreview Allocation-free snapshot of calling the next wave now; obtaining it does not mutate the simulation or emit events. SimEvent A value event. Value is damage or state total; IntValue is a slot, wave, or state delta. SimSystemInfo Immutable metadata for one pipeline entry, in actual execution order. No mutable system instance is exposed. StateHasher Stable FNV-1a value hashing with explicit byte order; never uses runtime object or string hashes. TargetQuery A target request using the shared elliptical distance metric. Vec2 A simulation-space vector independent of any engine. Interfaces IAbilityAction A custom ability payload; keep its immutable configuration here and per-entity state in custom components. ICommandCodec Optional persistence for custom commands. Type IDs 1024 and above belong to applications. ICommandHandler<T> Handles an exact custom command type without reflection or dynamic dispatch generation in the tick. ICustomComponent A prewarmed custom component; its reset must not allocate. IDamageHook Damage hooks run in registration order. Implementations must not allocate or recursively request damage in BeforeDamage. ISimProfiler Optional observational profiling hooks. Preallocate storage, avoid allocation, and do not mutate the world from callbacks. IStateHashContributor Optional deterministic state hashing for custom components, commands, systems, and other extension state. ITargetSelector Optional ranged target selection. Return null to decline an attack; use Simulation.FindDefaultTarget for fallback rather than recursively calling FindTarget. Enums CommandFailure Machine-readable command failure reasons. DamageOrigin Native request origin. Reflected packets are leaves and cannot trigger reflection or life steal again. DeploymentPhase Observable automatic-deployment preparation. EntityKind Stable system index categories. GamePhase Terminal and running game states. MechanicEndReason Stable reason codes used by deployment and channel end events. ResolutionKind A unit's one-time resolution cause; live units have None. RevivalPhase Same-identity down/rise state; only Active may move or attack. SimEventKind View-facing notifications in simulation processing order. SimStage Stable anchors for systems registered before the first tick.

reference/TDMaker.Editor.LevelDryRun.htm.title: Class LevelDryRun | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Editor.LevelDryRun.htm.summary: Class LevelDryRun Namespace TDMaker.Editor Assembly TDMaker.Editor.dll Headless content check: bakes a level and runs the simulation without rendering. The undefended run calls every wave as early as possible with no towers (shows total threat); the fortified run builds and upgrades towers on every slot with unlimited gold, buys every tower ability, spawns the level's heroes (moving them to the front enemy and spending skill points), and casts ready spells at the leading enemy (checks that every build, branch, rally, ability, move and cast is accepted and that the level can be completed). The budget pass plays with the level's real starting gold: it starts the first wave, lets later waves arrive on their timers and spends gold greedily (builds slots in list order, cycling the buildable towers, then the cheapest upgrade, branch or ability rank), with the same hero and spell assistance (checks that a sensible defense wins). public static class LevelDryRun Inheritance object reference/TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreensho.title: Class SampleScreenshot | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreensho.summary: Class SampleScreenshot Namespace TDMaker.Editor Assembly TDMaker.Editor.dll Plays the sample scene with a scripted run (build on every slot, upgrade, call waves early) and renders the main camera, HUD included, to a PNG (for store-page drafts). Works from the menu and from batch mode (-batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot.Capture, without -quit: the editor exits by itself). Needs a graphics device, so it does nothing under -nographics. Options: -tdmSeconds N (game seconds, default 50), -tdmWidth/-tdmHeight (default 1920x1080), -tdmOut folder (default .work/screenshots), -tdmScene path (default the Basic sample scene), -tdmName file (PNG name without extension), -tdmGold N (starting gold, default 4000), -tdmUpgradeEvery S (game seconds between scripted upgrades, default 1.5), -tdmCallEvery S (game seconds between early wave calls, default 8) -tdmSlots N (build on the first N pads only, default all), -tdmNoHud (map only, for key art) and -tdmShot mode: beam (default: waits for a channelled beam or chain lightning), barracks (waits for soldiers blocking several enemies), hero (sends the hero to the fight and casts every ready spell just before the shot) or worldmap (alias levelselect: the demo scene's world map with preview progress in a throw-away slot; use with the demo scene) or title (the title and its language buttons), or slots (the demo scene's save slot page over the same throw-away store) or shop (the world map's star-upgrade shop over the same throw-away slot, with a few ranks bought and one rank's tooltip shown). -tdmMenu build opens the build menu on the first pad left empty by -tdmSlots instead of a tower panel; -tdmHidePause keeps the frozen capture from showing the paused state. -tdmDemoLevel N starts battle N of the demo scene through its flow (instead of driving the scene's own runner); -tdmPanel opens a tower panel in every shot mode (normally only the beam mode shows one). -tdmLang code (for example ko) shows the HUD and menus in that language of the scene's text tables (not saved to PlayerPrefs). Demo-scene modes levelinfo (the world map with a level's info panel open) and controls (the How to Play page); -tdmPauseMenu opens the pause menu in battle shots. Script errors logged during the run are counted and reported, so the batch run doubles as a play-mode smoke test. reference/TDMaker.Editor.html.title: Namespace TDMaker.Editor | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Editor.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Editor Classes AudioCuePreview Previews AudioCues in the editor (edit mode or play mode) through one hidden AudioSource: a random clip and pitch per play, like AudioCuePlayer. Shared by inspectors and editor windows (the Audio section of authoring tools). BuildSlotAuthoringEditor Inspector and scene handles for BuildSlotAuthoring: rally point handle, preview tower range and rally radius (simulation ellipse), and a warning when the rally point lies outside the rally radius. CampaignAssetEditor Inspector of CampaignAsset: a map view of the world map picture with the level points and their unlock roads (arrows from prerequisites, dashed for branches, red for problems). Click a point to select it, drag it to move it, click an empty spot to move the selected point there, drop Level assets on the map to add them, right-click a point for more. Below: the ordered level list, the selected level's settings and the validation results. Every edit is undoable. CampaignEditing Editing helpers for CampaignAsset shared by the inspector, the New Level wizard and tests. CombatMath Editor-side estimates of combat numbers. Mirrors the simulation's reduction rules (physical, magical, explosion/electric at half physical, poison, true) but ignores rounding, status effects and incoming-damage multipliers, so values are approximate ("≈"). EditorWindowLayout Predictable initial utility-window placement without restoring a full-screen layout. EnemyAssetEditor Grouped inspector for EnemyAsset with effective HP and damage estimates. LevelAssetEditor Inspector actions for level assets. LevelAuthoringEditor Inspector actions for scene level authoring. LevelContext Finds the level a tower belongs to, so editor previews use the level's rules (for example the sale refundShare) instead of per-tower legacy values. LevelDryRun Headless content check: bakes a level and runs the simulation without rendering. The undefended run calls every wave as early as possible with no towers (shows total threat); the fortified run builds and upgrades towers on every slot with unlimited gold, buys every tower ability, spawns the level's heroes (moving them to the front enemy and spending skill points), and casts ready spells at the leading enemy (checks that every build, branch, rally, ability, move and cast is accepted and that the level can be completed). The budget pass plays with the level's real starting gold: it starts the first wave, lets later waves arrive on their timers and spends gold greedily (builds slots in list order, cycling the buildable towers, then the cheapest upgrade, branch or ability rank), with the same hero and spell assistance (checks that a sensible defense wins). LevelSceneBuilder Builds a playable scene from caller-owned assets. No sample content is loaded unless explicitly supplied by the caller. MapBackgroundPreview Edit-mode stand-in for the painted map: a hidden, never-saved sprite object that shows the level's ground art in the Scene view while the Map Editor is open (the Level View only builds the ground in Play mode). It is removed before Play mode, assembly reloads and when the Map Editor closes, so scenes and builds never contain it. MapEditing Undoable level-authoring operations behind the Map Editor (and usable from your own editor scripts): edit points of curve and polyline paths, create/delete/duplicate/align build slots with automatic rally points, path order, painted background setup and baking scene geometry into a LevelAsset. MapEditorWindow Map Editor (Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Map Editor): turns a painted map into a level. Drop a sprite or texture as the background (the camera bounds fit it), draw smooth curved paths with a few clicks, place build slots with automatic rally points, set where each entrance's wave-call button appears, then Validate, Dry Run and Bake — all with Undo and in the Scene view (2D). MapSceneGUI Scene-view drawing and handles shared by the Map Editor and the Path Authoring inspector: road band (lanes plus the painted-road padding), every sub-lane, direction arrows, entry/exit markers, wave-call buttons and edit-point handles for curve and polyline paths. NewAssetDialog Small modal dialog of the Unit Workshop's New menu: asks for the asset name and the folder it is created in. The folder defaults to the current user level's Data folder, then a user content folder (DefaultFolder, or the last folder picked), never to the package's own sample folders unless the user picks one explicitly. NewLevelBuilder Headless core of Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > New Level: creates a level folder with a Level asset, a Wave Set, starter units (sample kit or Unit Workshop presets), a HUD theme and a sprite material, and a scene built by the sample scene builder (Simulation Runner, Level Authoring, one path across the frame, six build slots with rally points on the road, camera, Game HUD, Level View, audio and music players). The result passes the Project Validator and plays in the Dry Run: lost without towers, won with a defense. Usable from tests and -executeMethod; the window only collects the settings. NewLevelResult What Create(NewLevelSettings) made. NewLevelSettings Inputs of Create(NewLevelSettings). NewLevelWizardWindow Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > New Level: collects a level name, a folder, an optional painted map, the starter content and the number of waves, then runs Create(NewLevelSettings). Afterwards the new scene is open, its Level is selected, the Map Editor is open on the path tool and the window shows the next steps. OnlineDocumentation Online manual entry points shared by the editor tools. PathAuthoringEditor Inspector and scene editor for PathAuthoring: drag points, Shift+click to add or insert, Ctrl+click to delete, Delete/Ctrl+D/F on the selected point, optional snapping, all sub-lanes, direction arrows, entry/exit markers, per-point lane width handles and build-slot range context. PathEditing Undoable point operations that keep per-point lane widths and entry/exit indices in sync. ProjectValidator Scans 2D Tower Defense Maker content in the project and open scenes: missing references, duplicate template ids, path and lane problems, waves referencing missing enemies or paths, upgrade cycles and unreachable upgrade tiers, level bake failures, missing TextMesh Pro Essential Resources, string table problems and campaign problems (missing levels, duplicate keys, unlock cycles, levels that can never open). RangePreview Scene-view drawing of range ellipses using exactly the simulation's shape (RangeShape), with the range Y scale resolved from the open scene's level and runner. SampleAudio Assigns the optional sample audio (Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Audio/Sfx/<key>.ogg and Music/<key>.ogg) to sample cues by key. A missing file leaves its cue empty, so sample generation is deterministic with or without the audio. The key tables are public so tests (and buyers copying the scheme) can check them. SampleBrowserWindow Separate entry point for optional examples and the complete sample game. SampleCatalog Optional sample locations. The Maker works without these assets or their generator. SampleContentGenerator Generates the "Basic" sample: projectiles, enemies, soldiers, four tower families, five waves on two multi-lane paths, status effects (slow, poison, stun, rally buff, shield ward), purchasable abilities on final branches (including a chain-lightning ability, a knockback ability, a channelled beam, a path-transfer rift and a trap-laying barracks), a support enemy with a shield cast and a permanent pulse-only healing aura, an armored enemy that reflects damage, one hero (with life steal and a trap skill), two spells (reinforcement and area strike), a level asset and a ready-to-play scene. All content is original and uses hand-authored vector art with procedural fallbacks; the scene uses the uGUI GameHud with a theme asset, a fitted camera, a painted ground and the IMGUI HUD as an F1 debug overlay. Re-running updates the existing assets in place. The same run also generates the Crossroads and Winding Pass levels (which reuse the Basic towers, enemies and hero) and the Demo scene (title, level select, pause and result flow over all three levels), plus the English and Korean sample string tables (Samples/Text) that every sample scene's Game Settings use, and the dynamic Korean fallback font asset of the sample HUD themes (Samples/Fonts). SampleScreenshot Plays the sample scene with a scripted run (build on every slot, upgrade, call waves early) and renders the main camera, HUD included, to a PNG (for store-page drafts). Works from the menu and from batch mode (-batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot.Capture, without -quit: the editor exits by itself). Needs a graphics device, so it does nothing under -nographics. Options: -tdmSeconds N (game seconds, default 50), -tdmWidth/-tdmHeight (default 1920x1080), -tdmOut folder (default .work/screenshots), -tdmScene path (default the Basic sample scene), -tdmName file (PNG name without extension), -tdmGold N (starting gold, default 4000), -tdmUpgradeEvery S (game seconds between scripted upgrades, default 1.5), -tdmCallEvery S (game seconds between early wave calls, default 8) -tdmSlots N (build on the first N pads only, default all), -tdmNoHud (map only, for key art) and -tdmShot mode: beam (default: waits for a channelled beam or chain lightning), barracks (waits for soldiers blocking several enemies), hero (sends the hero to the fight and casts every ready spell just before the shot) or worldmap (alias levelselect: the demo scene's world map with preview progress in a throw-away slot; use with the demo scene) or title (the title and its language buttons), or slots (the demo scene's save slot page over the same throw-away store) or shop (the world map's star-upgrade shop over the same throw-away slot, with a few ranks bought and one rank's tooltip shown). -tdmMenu build opens the build menu on the first pad left empty by -tdmSlots instead of a tower panel; -tdmHidePause keeps the frozen capture from showing the paused state. -tdmDemoLevel N starts battle N of the demo scene through its flow (instead of driving the scene's own runner); -tdmPanel opens a tower panel in every shot mode (normally only the beam mode shows one). -tdmLang code (for example ko) shows the HUD and menus in that language of the scene's text tables (not saved to PlayerPrefs). Demo-scene modes levelinfo (the world map with a level's info panel open) and controls (the How to Play page); -tdmPauseMenu opens the pause menu in battle shots. Script errors logged during the run are counted and reported, so the batch run doubles as a play-mode smoke test. ScenePreview Shared scene-view context drawing for level authoring: build slots, rally points, rally radius and tower range ellipses (same shape the simulation tests). Toggles persist in editor preferences. TDEditorGUI Shared colors, styles and small IMGUI helpers for the 2D Tower Defense Maker editor tools. TemplateInspectorBase Base for grouped template inspectors: draws named property groups in persistent foldouts and any fields not claimed by a group under "Other", so new serialized fields never disappear from the inspector. TextMeshProSetup TextMesh Pro setup check. The HUD, damage numbers and sample menus use TextMesh Pro (part of the uGUI package in Unity 6), which needs its "Essential Resources" (default font asset, shaders, settings) imported into the project once. 2D Tower Defense Maker does not ship those resources. When they are missing this class logs one clear message per editor session, offers a one-click import in a dialog, and is available as Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Import TMP Essential Resources (also used by the Validator). TowerAssetEditor Grouped inspector for TowerAsset with DPS vs armor, range ellipse and upgrade economics. TowerTree Project-wide queries and undoable edits on tower upgrade graphs. UnitFrames Bulk frame registration for the Unit Workshop: sorts sprite files into walk / idle / attack / hurt / death sequences by file name ("Orc_Walk_003", "walk (2)", "1_ATTACK_005", "goblinRun07", "Hit1"), fixes their texture import settings (single sprite, pivot at the feet, compressed) and writes the sequences into an ArtSet.Entry. Facing is never guessed; the author ticks Faces Left. UnitMath Unit Workshop numbers that follow the simulation's integer damage rules exactly (single-target hits without status effects or incoming multipliers): a hit rolls ceil(lerp(min, max, u)), projectile hits deal at least 1, the target keeps floor(rolled × (1 − reduction)) (soldiers: round(rolled − floor(rolled × reduction))), and the reduction is the matching defense minus pierce (explosion and electric use half the physical armor), clamped to [0, 1]. Ratio checks use the bands of the balance notes (new content starting points, not rules). UnitPresets Fills enemy, hero and soldier assets from ratios to a baseline (the project's median enemy and soldier, or built-in defaults). The ratios stay inside the bands of the balance notes: bounty density ×0.5–1.8 of the baseline, defenses in the low (0–0.2), medium (0.2–0.5) and strong (0.5–0.7) bands, hero experience steps ×1.1–1.6 after a first jump of ×2.5–3.5. They are a starting point; tune the result against your own towers. UnitReferences Reverse lookups for the Unit Workshop: which levels, waves, towers and other assets use a unit, projectile or effect. UnitSandbox The Unit Workshop's test range: a straight lane with the chosen towers beside it, and a wave of the unit under test (or, for heroes and soldiers, a wave of an opponent enemy against them). Run(Setup) plays it headless and deterministically (fixed seed, fixed tick); BuildLevel(Setup, List<Object>) returns the same level for the play-mode sandbox. UnitSandbox.Result Outcome of a headless run. UnitSandbox.Setup What to test. UnitSandboxPlay Play-mode sandbox of the Unit Workshop: opens a new unsaved scene (camera, runner, views, debug HUD), enters Play mode, then rebuilds the sandbox level in play mode (so nothing depends on objects surviving the domain reload), builds every tower and calls the wave. Nothing is written to disk. When Play mode stops, the scenes that were open before (saved scenes only) are opened again. UnitWorkshopWindow Unit Workshop (Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Unit Workshop): enemies, heroes, soldiers, towers, projectiles, status effects and spells in one window. A searchable list (create from presets, duplicate, rename, delete, see who uses an asset), an animation preview (art set frames, Faces Left check, health bar, pivot, projectile flight), tabbed flat forms (basics, attacks, mechanic cards, effects and tags, look with bulk frame registration, hero growth, audio, engagement places), computed values that follow the simulation's damage rules, and a sandbox that plays the unit against chosen towers. Edits use Undo; several selected assets of one type are edited together. UpgradeShopAssetEditor Inspector of UpgradeShopAsset: a button to the Upgrade Shop window, the validation list and the default fields. UpgradeShopWindow Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop: edits an UpgradeShopAsset as a grid (tracks as columns, ranks as cells). Add, remove and reorder tracks and ranks, fill a track's prices from its first and last price with a back-loaded curve, edit the selected rank's effects (each with a readable summary), preview a tower's, unit's or spell's stats before and after the upgrades with the core rewriter, and see the validation problems. Every edit is undoable. UpgradeTreeLayout Hand-moved node positions of the Upgrade Tree window, per tree (root tower) and node (tower asset GUIDs). Editor-only: kept in UserSettings/ of the project, never in the assets or a build. UpgradeTreeWindow Graph view of a tower's upgrade tree (level 1 → 2 → 3 → branches). Each node shows its cost, cumulative investment and sell refund; clicking a node edits it inline. Nodes can grow new levels or branches, which are created as assets next to their parent. Drag a node to move it (the offset is kept per tree in the project's UserSettings, editor only); drag the empty canvas, or use the middle mouse button, to pan. ValidationIssue One problem found by ProjectValidator. ValidatorWindow Lists ProjectValidator issues with filters; click to select, double-click to open the right tool. WaveSchedule Mirrors the simulation's spawn schedule: a group's entries run back to back; an entry entered at s with start delay d, interval h and count n spawns at s+d+h … s+d+nh, waits one more interval, then the next entry is entered after the following gap. WaveTimelineWindow Timeline editor for WaveSetAssets. Each wave group is a row (sorted by path); each spawn entry is a bar from its start delay to its last wait, with a tick per spawn, colored by enemy. Drag bars to change delays, drag the right edge to change the interval (Shift: count), and edit the selection in the side inspector. With Follow on it shows the waves of the selected Wave Set / Level asset, or of the Level Authoring selected in (or present in) the open scene. WelcomeWindow Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Welcome: first stop after importing the package – check (and import) the TextMesh Pro Essential Resources, start an independent new level, browse optional examples, and open the Unit Workshop or the Map Editor. Shown automatically the first time a project loads the package, and then at each editor start while Show on startup is on (per project). WorkshopDirtyState Remembers the last saved (clean) state of the assets an editor window edits, so that Undo back to that state clears the "modified" mark again (Unity keeps an asset dirty after Undo), and so that unsaved edits can be discarded on request. Snapshots are taken once per clean period (when an asset is first seen not dirty), not every frame. WorkshopGUI IMGUI helpers of the Unit Workshop: flat forms (nested data drawn as labelled blocks instead of nested foldouts, with enabled / useX switches hiding what is off), cards and small drawing utilities. Structs EntrySpan Timing of one spawn entry inside its group, in seconds from the wave start. LevelDryRun.PassResult Outcome of one pass. UnitFrames.Classified Result of classifying one file name. UnitFrames.Report Summary of a bulk registration. UnitMath.HeroRow One growth row of a hero, as the bake computes it. UnitMath.KillEstimate Kill estimate of one tower tier against one unit. UnitMath.Outlier A value outside its usual band. UnitPresets.Baseline Reference numbers a preset scales. UnitReferences.Use One user of an asset. UnitSandbox.SourceRow Damage dealt by one source template. WaveTotals Aggregate numbers for a wave. Enums FrameAction Animation a sprite file belongs to, guessed from its name by Classify(string). IssueSeverity Severity of a validation issue. LevelDryRun.Pass The three passes of a dry run. MapEditorWindow.Tool The Map Editor's Scene-view tools. StarterContent What the New Level wizard puts into a new level. UnitPreset Starting points offered by the Unit Workshop's New menu. UnitSandbox.Verdict How a sandbox run ended, judged by what reached the exit (the test level has spare lives, so its phase alone says little). UnitWorkshopWindow.Kind Asset families shown in the list. UnitWorkshopWindow.MechanicCard The mechanic cards the Mechanics tab can add (unit traits, on-hit payloads and timed action payloads). UnitWorkshopWindow.Tab Edit panel tabs.

reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.Engage.title: Class EngagementHostData | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.Engage.summary: Class EngagementHostData Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Authoring Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Where blockers stand around this enemy (the engagement host). Blockers stand on the side the enemy is walking toward, host X + guest X world units away horizontally, shifted by the summed Y values. The second and third blocker take rows at −/+ rowSpacing on Y (pulled back by half of it on X); later blockers repeat the three places. Independent of melee range. Typical X: half the enemy's drawn body width plus a small gap. public sealed class EngagementHostData Inheritance object EngagementHostData Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors EngagementHostData() public EngagementHostData() Fields contactBias This enemy's share of the horizontal gap (X, at least 0) and a signed world-Y shift (Y). [Tooltip("This enemy's share of the horizontal distance to its blockers (X ≥ 0) and a signed world-Y shift (Y). Usually half the drawn body width plus a small gap.")] public Vector2 contactBias Field Value Vector2 rowSpacing World-Y distance of the second and third blocker rows. [Tooltip("World-Y distance of the second and third blockers' rows; they also stand half of it closer on X.")] [Min(0.01)] public float rowSpacing Field Value float Methods ToDef() Bakes the host geometry (the guest share keeps its default; it comes from the blocker's own template). public MeleeEngagementDef ToDef() Returns MeleeEngagementDef

reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MineFi.title: Class MineFieldData | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MineFi.summary: Class MineFieldData Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Authoring Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Automatic mine laying, baked into a DeploymentPlanDef with a TrapDef payload. Each activation picks one lane node of a level path inside the distance band around the producer (seeded, deterministic), reserves it, throws the mine (flight, landing, then the arm delay) and leaves a trap that bursts under the first eligible unit. The lifetime counts from the throw. Use it as an ability action (useMines); it fails, without a fallback spot, when no node fits. public sealed class MineFieldData Inheritance object MineFieldData Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors MineFieldData() public MineFieldData() Fields area Optional region left where the mine bursts. [Tooltip("Optional region (effect and/or pulse) left at the mine on every trigger.")] public AreaEffectData area Field Value AreaEffectData armDelay Delay after landing before the mine can trigger. [Tooltip("Arming delay after the landing preparation.")] [Min(0)] public float armDelay Field Value float color Marker, detection ring and blast colour. [Header("Look")] public Color color Field Value Color damage Hit on trigger: an area packet is centred on the mine, a single-target packet hits the triggering unit. [Tooltip("Hit on trigger: an area packet (radius > 0) is centred on the mine and re-searches its victims; radius 0 hits only the triggering unit.")] public DamageData damage Field Value DamageData id Event key: selects the marker colour and the keyed audio cue, and counts toward the mine limit. [Tooltip("Event key: selects the marker colour and the keyed audio cue, and counts toward the mine limit.")] public string id Field Value string keepWhenSourceLost Mines stay when their producer is sold or dies (off = they are removed with it). [Tooltip("Mines already laid stay when the producer is sold, dies or disappears (their kill credit is kept).")] public bool keepWhenSourceLost Field Value bool lifetime Total lifetime from the throw, including flight, landing and arming. [Tooltip("Lifetime in game seconds from the throw (flight, landing and arming count). An unused mine fades out without exploding.")] [Min(0.05)] public float lifetime Field Value float maxMines Maximum live and in-flight mines of this producer; a full field rejects the throw. [Tooltip("Maximum mines of this id alive or in flight per producer. A full field rejects the throw (old mines are never replaced). 0 = no limit.")] [Min(0)] public int maxMines Field Value int maxTriggers Activations before the mine is used up. [Tooltip("Activations before the mine is used up (1 = a single blast).")] [Min(1)] public int maxTriggers Field Value int maximumDistance Outer radius of the placement band (range ellipse). [Tooltip("Outer radius of the placement band (range ellipse); usually a little less than the producer's attack range.")] [Min(0)] public float maximumDistance Field Value float minimumDistance Inner radius of the placement band around the producer (range ellipse). [Header("Placement")] [Tooltip("Inner radius of the placement band around the producer (range ellipse). Lane nodes closer than this are skipped.")] [Min(0)] public float minimumDistance Field Value float minimumSpacing Minimum distance between mines, including mines still in flight. [Tooltip("Minimum distance between mines, including those still in flight. About half to one detection diameter spreads them out.")] [Min(0)] public float minimumSpacing Field Value float pointRule Terrain check for candidate nodes; a node the rule moves is rejected. [Tooltip("Terrain check for every candidate lane node (for example bounds). A node the rule would move is skipped.")] public PointRuleData pointRule Field Value PointRuleData settleDuration Landing preparation before the arming delay. [Tooltip("Landing preparation after the flight, before the arming delay.")] [Min(0)] public float settleDuration Field Value float sideClearance Minimum horizontal offset from the producer (keeps mines off the spot right under it). [Tooltip("Minimum horizontal (X) offset of a site from the producer; 0 accepts sites straight above or below it.")] [Min(0)] public float sideClearance Field Value float spacingScope Spacing counts only this producer's mines, or every deployment. [Tooltip("Owner: spacing only against this producer's mines. Global: against every deployment (other producers and spell traps).")] public DeploymentSpacingScope spacingScope Field Value DeploymentSpacingScope targets Extra trigger eligibility (blast victims use normal damage eligibility). public MechanicTargetData targets Field Value MechanicTargetData targetsEnemies Triggered by enemies (otherwise by friendly soldiers and heroes). [Tooltip("Triggered by enemies (off = by friendly soldiers and heroes, for mines laid by enemies).")] public bool targetsEnemies Field Value bool targetsFlying Flying units can trigger it. public bool targetsFlying Field Value bool targetsGround Ground units can trigger it. public bool targetsGround Field Value bool transitDuration Flight time before the landing. [Tooltip("Flight time of the throw (drawn as an arc).")] [Min(0)] public float transitDuration Field Value float triggerRadius Detection radius (range ellipse), usually a fraction of the blast radius. [Tooltip("Detection radius (range ellipse). reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.html.title: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Authoring | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Authoring Classes AbilityActionAsset Base class for ScriptableObjects that provide a custom IAbilityAction to an ability, skill or behavior action (customAction). The created action is shared by every entity using the asset, so keep it immutable and store per-entity state in a custom component. AbilityActionData One timed action channel of an ability rank, baked into AbilityActionDef. Payloads can be combined. AbilityData A purchasable tower ability or a hero skill with one or more ranks. AbilityRankData The complete payload of one ability or skill rank. Each rank replaces the previous rank's payload. AreaEffectData A timed region that attaches an effect to occupants and/or pulses damage or healing, baked into AreaEffectDef. Leave effect empty and enable pulse for a pulse-only region. AreaPulseData A direct damage and/or healing pulse on every occupant of a region, baked into AreaPulseDef. A region whose status effect is empty becomes a pulse-only region. AudioCue A sound hook: one of several clips played with a random pitch. Empty cues are silent, so every slot is optional. Cues are routed through TDMaker.Unity.View.AudioCuePlayer (pooled AudioSources). BakedLevel The result of baking a level: core inputs plus lookups back to authoring assets for the view. BasicDamageData A damage packet without an impact payload, baked into DamageDef. Used where a payload would nest (secondary blasts, region pulses); attacks use DamageData, which adds impact. BeamData A continuous single-target channel with an exact total damage budget split over pulses, baked into BeamDef. Use it as an ability action (useBeam). The view draws a pooled line for its whole duration. BuildSlotAuthoring Scene authoring for a construction slot. The rally point is stored as an offset from the slot. BuildSlotData A construction slot with its default barracks rally point. CameraFramingData Per-level camera framing for maps larger than the screen: how much of the map one screen shows, where the view starts and an optional intro pan along the first path. Read by TDCameraController; presentation only (no simulation effect). ChainAttackData A chained attack that jumps from target to nearby target without revisiting, baked into ChainAttackDef. Use it as an ability action (useChain). ClickAreaSettings Per-content override of the HUD's click target: an axis-aligned world rectangle around the entity position (the interior is clickable, the border is not) and a priority added to the kind's default (heroes 1, everything else 0). When several targets contain the click, the higher priority wins, then the lower world reference point. CombatModifierData Reversible combat changes carried by a status effect or passive, baked into CombatModifierDef. CompanionData Owner-bound companion slots on a hero or tower, baked into a CompanionDef (template custom data). Each slot keeps one child alive: a ground escort (an ordinary soldier that blocks and follows the owner's move or rally orders) or a flying follower (keeps near the owner, never blocks, attacks from where it is). A fallen child is replaced after refillDelay, counted from its death. Child damage earns the owner experience. CompositeAbilityAction Runs several custom actions as one channel payload; succeeds when any of them succeeds. DamageData Serializable damage packet baked into DamageDef, with an optional impact payload. DeathSuccessionData Extra rules for the enemies released by deathSummon (successors), baked with WithDeathSuccession(int, float, SuccessorBountyPolicy, bool, bool): a shared chain budget (successors of successors), a rise time and the bounty rule. A lineage never pays its bounty twice and leaks only once. EnemyAsset A path-following hostile unit. EngagementGuestData Where this soldier or hero stands when it blocks an enemy (the engagement guest): its share of the horizontal gap, added to the enemy's share. See EngagementHostData. EngagementHostData Where blockers stand around this enemy (the engagement host). Blockers stand on the side the enemy is walking toward, host X + guest X world units away horizontally, shifted by the summed Y values. The second and third blocker take rows at −/+ rowSpacing on Y (pulled back by half of it on X); later blockers repeat the three places. Independent of melee range. Typical X: half the enemy's drawn body width plus a small gap. EntityAssetBase Base class for ScriptableObjects that bake into a core EntityTemplate. HealingData Health restoration, baked into HealingDef. Not affected by damage multipliers or defenses. HeroAsset A player-controlled hero: base stats, growth rows (experience → level → skill points), skills and respawn. Add it to heroes; the runner spawns it at the level's hero spawn point. HeroLevelData One hero growth row. Values scale the hero's base stats to produce the absolute row the simulation uses. ImpactPayloadData Extra work after a resolved hit, baked into ImpactPayloadDef: a secondary blast, a residual region (which may be pulse-only) and/or a path displacement (negative distance = knockback toward the entry). LaneBuilder Generates parallel sub-lanes by offsetting a center line along mitred normals. LevelAsset A complete level: geometry, waves, economy and the towers the player may build. Call Bake() to produce a TemplateRegistry and LevelDef. LevelAuthoring Combines a LevelAsset (waves, economy, towers) with scene geometry from PathAuthoring and BuildSlotAuthoring components. Empty lists are filled from children in hierarchy order. LevelMusicData Music of one level, played by TDMaker.Unity.View.MusicPlayer: a battle loop, an optional intense loop for late or boss waves, and victory / defeat stingers that stop or duck the loop. Empty clips fall back to the music player's defaults, so every field is optional. LevelRulesData Level-wide economy and flow rules, baked into LevelRulesDef. LifeStealData Heals the attacker (or the hero credited with the hit) by a share of the health this packet actually removed, baked into LifeStealDef. MechanicTargetData Extra recipient eligibility for mechanic actions, baked into MechanicTargetDef. Defaults accept everyone. MechanicVisual View-side look of a keyed mechanic (chain, multi-target attack, region pulse, trap, mines, beam, transfer, reflection, life steal, body raising), collected while baking. MeleeData Serializable melee attack; disabled data bakes to no melee slot. MineFieldData Automatic mine laying, baked into a DeploymentPlanDef with a TrapDef payload. Each activation picks one lane node of a level path inside the distance band around the producer (seeded, deterministic), reserves it, throws the mine (flight, landing, then the arm delay) and leaves a trap that bursts under the first eligible unit. The lifetime counts from the throw. Use it as an ability action (useMines); it fails, without a fallback spot, when no node fits. MultiTargetAttackData One activation that hits several distinct targets at once, baked into MultiTargetAttackDef. Towers pick targets by their current priority; other actors pick the nearest first. PathAuthoring Scene authoring for an enemy path. Points are in local space; sub-lanes are generated from the center line using laneCount and laneSpacing. In curve mode (curve) the user edits a few controlPoints and points is regenerated as a smooth curve sampled every curveNodeSpacing units (see RebuildFromCurve()). PathData A path authored as a center line; parallel sub-lanes are generated from it. PathDestinationData An exact point on a level path, baked into PathDestinationDef. Validated against the level when used: an invalid destination (path, lane or node outside the path's entry..exit range) moves nothing. PathGeometry Authoring geometry helpers: smooth curves (centripetal Catmull-Rom) sampled into simulation nodes, and nearest-point queries on path center lines. Used by PathAuthoring curve mode and the editor's Map Editor. PathTransferData Moves nearby path-following enemies to an exact path destination (a rift, a recall), baked into PathTransferDef. Use it as an ability action (useTransfer); hits can transfer through useTransfer. PeriodicDamageData Damage over time with integer rolls, baked into PeriodicDamageDef. PeriodicHealingData Periodic healing carried by a status effect, baked into PeriodicHealingDef. PointRuleData Shared placement validation for spells and hero movement, baked into PointRuleDef. PresentationHooks Optional per-template presentation hooks: VFX prefabs (pooled) and audio cues for the standard moments of a unit's life. Every field may be left empty. ProjectileAsset Projectile travel and presentation data shared by ranged attacks. RaiseRemainsData Raises new units from the bodies the fallen leave behind, baked into a RaiseRemainsDef. Each activation reserves the closest eligible bodies (ties by body order), casts for castDelay, then consumes each body and creates unit there (an enemy continues the body's path; a soldier fights for the player). A moved, stunned or dead caster releases its reservations. Bodies decay after the runner's Remains Lifetime. Use it as an ability action (useRaise). RangeShape The single source of the range ellipse used by every view, gizmo and editor preview. It matches the simulation (Simulation.RangeDistanceSquared): a point is inside when dx²/r² + dy²/(k·r)² ≤ 1 (boundary included), with k = range Y scale. The horizontal semi-axis is r and the vertical semi-axis is k·r, so k < 1 flattens the ellipse vertically (an oblique top-down look). RangedAttackData Serializable ranged attack channel. RecoveryData Health recovery, baked into RecoveryDef. ReflectionData Returns a share of the health actually lost by this unit to its attacker as a single hit, baked into ReflectionDef. Shield absorption and overkill do not count; reflected hits never reflect again or steal life. ReviveData Same-unit return on the spot, baked into a ReviveDef (template custom data): a killed unit lies down, then gets returnShare of its health back, rises and walks on with the same identity. Its bounty is paid once, on the first death. Pending returns hold victory. ShieldData A damage-absorbing shield carried by a status effect, baked into ShieldDef. SoldierAsset A friendly unit produced by a barracks tower to block enemies. SpawnEntryData A timed run of identical enemies inside a wave group. SpellAsset A player spell with a cooldown and a target point. Bakes to SpellDef; list it in spells. The point rule is shared by the HUD preview and the cast command. StarRatingData Legacy (0.x) view-side star rule, kept only so older level assets load. The rating is now computed by the core from victoryRating; LevelAsset migrates these values into it on load. StatModifierData Reversible stat changes, baked into StatModifierDef. Identity values bake to no modifier. StatusEffectAsset An attached status effect (slow, stun, armor shift, damage over time ...). Bakes to StatusEffectDef. Reference it from attack damage (effects), area effects, abilities or spells. StrikeData Scattered, individually timed area strikes for one cast, baked into StrikeSequenceDef. SummonData A unit sequence for spells, abilities and death emissions, baked into SummonDef. TagMask Converts the 32-bit tag masks shown in the Inspector to the core's 64-bit tag bits. TemplateExtensionAsset Base class for ScriptableObjects that decorate a baked template, for example with WithCustomData. List them in an entity asset's extensions; they run in list order during the level bake. TowerAsset A buildable tower tier. Each tier is its own asset; upgrades lists the next tiers (more than one entry is a branch). A tower with a soldier acts as a barracks. TrapData A fixed-position deployment (mine, snare, glyph) placed by an ability action, baked into TrapDef. It arms after a delay, then hits the nearest eligible unit inside its detection radius until its triggers or lifetime run out. Use it as an ability action (useTrap). VictoryRatingData Victory star bands by the share of starting lives left (inclusive): at or above threeStarLifeRatio = 3 stars, at or above twoStarLifeRatio = 2 stars, otherwise 1. Bakes to VictoryRatingDef. ViewSettings How an entity is presented. A prefab wins; otherwise a generated primitive sprite is used. WaveData One wave and its call timing. WaveGroupData Spawn entries that share a path and a start delay. WaveSetAsset An ordered list of waves. Enums AudioChannel Volume channel of a sound. Every cue and music track is scaled by Master and its own channel (see TDMaker.Unity.View.TDGameSettings), and routed to that channel's optional AudioMixerGroup. CameraFramingMode How the game camera frames a level on start (see CameraFramingData). CameraStartFocus Where the camera looks when the level starts. FacingMode How a view mirrors itself to face its movement direction. MechanicVisualKind What a MechanicVisual belongs to, where the view treats it specially. PrimitiveShape Generated placeholder shapes used when no prefab is assigned. SpellKind Main payload of a player spell.

reference/TDMaker.Unity.Campaign.Campaig.summary: Class CampaignProgress Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Campaign Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Campaign rules over one save slot's ProfileData. A level is locked until its record exists; records are created when the unlock rule holds (Refresh()), and an opened level never locks again. A victory is first recorded as a pending clear (RecordVictory(string, int), at the end of the battle) and merged into the map once by ApplyPending() (on map entry): best stars keep the maximum, re-wins never grant stars twice, the first win raises FirstCleared, and the next levels open. Several victories before a merge keep the best rating, and a later defeat does not discard it. Earned stars = sum of best stars of the levels that count; available = earned − spent. public sealed class CampaignProgress Inheritance object CampaignProgress Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors CampaignProgress(CampaignAsset, ProfileData) Wraps data (null starts a new profile). public CampaignProgress(CampaignAsset campaign, ProfileData data = null) Parameters campaign CampaignAsset data ProfileData Properties AvailableStars Stars left to spend (earned − spent, never below 0). public int AvailableStars { get; } Property Value int Campaign The campaign. public CampaignAsset Campaign { get; } Property Value CampaignAsset Data The slot data this progress reads and changes (save it through the store). public ProfileData Data { get; } Property Value ProfileData EarnedStars Stars earned on the map: best stars of every campaign level that counts toward the total. public int EarnedStars { get; } Property Value int HasPending Whether victories wait to be merged into the map. public bool HasPending { get; } Property Value bool ProjectedStars Stars the slot will have once the pending victories are merged (for slot previews): each level counts the higher of its record and its pending rating, never both, capped by MaxStars. public int ProjectedStars { get; } Property Value int SpentStars Stars spent on permanent upgrades. public int SpentStars { get; set; } Property Value int Methods ApplyPending() Merges the pending victories into the map once and clears them: best stars keep the maximum, the first win completes the level (and raises FirstCleared), then every level whose rule now holds opens. Pending clears of unknown or still locked levels are dropped. Calling it again without new victories changes nothing. reference/TDMaker.Unity.Campaign.SaveLoa.summary: Enum SaveLoadStatus Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Campaign Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Outcome of reading a save slot. public enum SaveLoadStatus Fields Corrupt = 3 The content could not be read. It was kept as a backup and the slot starts empty. Empty = 0 The slot holds nothing. Failed = 5 The storage could not be read (I/O error, storage unavailable). Nothing was changed. reference/TDMaker.Unity.Campaign.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Campaign Classes CampaignAsset A campaign: ordered levels on a world map with unlock rules (previous level, a list of required levels, an optional star gate, side branches that never block the main path) and the map picture. Progress lives in a save slot (ProfileData, read through CampaignProgress); this asset only describes the campaign. Edit it in the inspector: click in the map view to place level points, and the inspector lists validation problems. CampaignLevel One level of a CampaignAsset: what to play, where its point sits on the world map and when it opens. CampaignMapScreen World map screen built from code (uGUI + TextMesh Pro, styled by a HudTheme): the campaign's map picture with a point per level (locked with a lock, open with its number, completed with its best stars), dashed roads from each level's prerequisites, the star total, and a level info panel (title, summary, best stars, unlock requirements, Play). Call Show(CampaignProgress, CampaignMapUpdate) with the slot's progress and the update returned by ApplyPending() to highlight new stars and newly opened levels. PlayRequested and BackRequested leave the screen to the caller. Keys: 1-9 select a level, Enter plays it, Esc closes the panel and then goes back. Texts use HudTexts keys and relabel when the language changes. When the campaign has an upgradeShop, a Shop button (with the unspent stars as a badge) opens the UpgradeShopScreen over the map. CampaignMapUpdate Everything a map should show after merging victories: new stars, first clears and newly opened levels. CampaignProgress Campaign rules over one save slot's ProfileData. A level is locked until its record exists; records are created when the unlock rule holds (Refresh()), and an opened level never locks again. A victory is first recorded as a pending clear (RecordVictory(string, int), at the end of the battle) and merged into the map once by ApplyPending() (on map entry): best stars keep the maximum, re-wins never grant stars twice, the first win raises FirstCleared, and the next levels open. Several victories before a merge keep the best rating, and a later defeat does not discard it. Earned stars = sum of best stars of the levels that count; available = earned − spent. CampaignSaveSlots Save slots of one campaign over an ISaveStore: summaries for the slot picker, opening a slot (creating a fresh profile for an empty or unreadable one), saving the active slot and deleting slots. App settings are not stored here. CampaignSession The save slots whose slot is open right now (set by Open(int)). A SimulationRunner reads the open slot's purchased upgrade ranks and its campaign's upgradeShop from here when a battle starts, and the upgrade shop saves through it, so a flow script needs no extra wiring. Cleared when play mode starts. CampaignUi Helpers shared by the campaign screens (built from code with a HudTheme, like the HUD). JsonFileSaveStore Default store: one JSON file per slot under UnityEngine.Application.persistentDataPath (folder TDMakerSaves, files slot1.json, slot2.json, ...). Writes go to a temporary file that then replaces the slot file, so a crash mid-write leaves the previous save intact. An unreadable file is renamed to slotN.json.bak (or .bak2, ...) and kept. Not for WebGL (use PlayerPrefsSaveStore, or CreateDefault(int, string)). LevelRecord Saved progress of one campaign level. A record exists once the level is open. MemorySaveStore In-memory store (nothing persists): for tests, previews and tools. PendingClear A victory recorded at the end of a battle and not yet merged into the map (see ApplyPending()). PlayerPrefsSaveStore Store in UnityEngine.PlayerPrefs (browser storage in WebGL builds): one string per slot under prefix + slot number. Unreadable content is copied to key.bak before the slot is cleared. Flushes with UnityEngine.PlayerPrefs.Save() on every write. ProfileData Everything one save slot stores: opened levels with best stars, victories not yet merged into the map, purchased permanent upgrade ranks per track, stars spent on them, and free game-specific entries. App settings (volumes, language) are not part of a slot; they stay in TDGameSettings. Serialized with UnityEngine.JsonUtility by ProfileSerializer; version drives migrations. ProfileEntry A game-specific value kept in the save slot (tutorial flags, selected hero, ...). ProfileSerializer JSON form of ProfileData with schema versions. Reading runs the built-in migration steps and then every registered Migrate step from the file's version up to CurrentVersion (JsonUtility leaves fields a file does not have at their defaults, so a step only fixes meaning, not shape). SaveSlotScreen Save slot picker built from code (styled by a HudTheme): one row per slot of a CampaignSaveSlots with its stars, levels won and last play time, a Continue / New Campaign button and Delete (with a confirmation dialog: Delete, Cancel). One click on a slot opens it (SlotChosen); a new slot needs no name or extra confirmation. Keys: 1-9 choose a slot, Esc cancels the dialog and then goes back. Texts use HudTexts keys. SaveStoreFactory Picks the store for the running platform. TextSaveStore Shared logic of the text-based stores: JSON through ProfileSerializer, unreadable or newer content moved to a backup before the slot is treated as empty, and exceptions turned into results with a warning. UpgradeEffectData One effect of an upgrade rank. Maps one to one to a core UpgradeEffectDef. UpgradeRankData One purchasable rank of a track: its star price and its effects (added on top of the lower ranks). UpgradeRankRecord Purchased rank of one permanent upgrade track (ranks below it count as owned). UpgradeShopAsset The permanent star-upgrade shop of a campaign: ordered tracks (columns) of ranks bought in order with earned stars. Purchases live in the save slot (GetUpgradeRank(string) by track key); a battle bakes the shop and the purchased ranks into a core UpgradeSnapshot (CreateSnapshot(Func<string, int>, int?)) that the simulation applies before anything spawns. Assign it to upgradeShop (the world map then shows a Shop button and every battle started while that campaign's slot is open applies it) or to a SimulationRunner directly. Edit it in Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop. UpgradeShopScreen The permanent star-upgrade shop, built from code (uGUI + TextMesh Pro, styled by a HudTheme) over the world map: one column per track with its rank nodes, the stars to spend, a tooltip on hover (price, state and an effect summary generated from the data), one click on the next affordable rank buys it at once (no confirmation), Undo Changes returns to the purchases the shop opened with, Reset All clears every purchase (no confirmation) and Done or Esc closes it. Every change is saved immediately (UpgradeShopSession). CampaignMapScreen opens it from its Shop button. UpgradeShopSession One visit of the star-upgrade shop over a save slot. Every rule comes from the core UpgradeShopRules: only the next rank of a track can be bought and only with enough stars (Available = EarnedTotal − Spent); opening the session copies the purchases as the revert baseline; Revert() returns to that baseline (not one step back); ResetAll() clears every purchase and makes the cleared state the new baseline. Each change is written into the slot's ProfileData (ranks per track key and stars spent) and saved at once through Save. UpgradeShopText Texts of the upgrade shop in the current language: track names and summaries (shop.track.<key>.name|summary, then the authored English), rank lines (shop.track.<key>.rank<N>) and effect summaries generated from the effect data ("Range +10%", "Cooldown -2s", "New: Shell Burst", "Conscript becomes Veteran"). UpgradeTargetData Which templates or spells an effect changes. Filters combine with AND; inside the asset list and inside the kind mask they are alternatives. Empty filters do not restrict (an effect with no filter at all changes everything of the field's kind). UpgradeTrackData One shop column: a chain of ranks bought in order. Structs CampaignIssue One problem found by Validate(). CampaignLevelChange What one ApplyPending() changed on a level. SaveSlotSummary What a slot picker shows for one slot without opening it. Interfaces ISaveStore Where save slots live. Implementations never throw from these calls: failures are reported through the return values (and a console warning). Slot numbers start at 0. Unreadable content is never deleted silently: it is kept as a backup. Enums CampaignIssueSeverity Severity of a CampaignIssue. CampaignLevelState Map state of a campaign level. CampaignUnlock How a campaign level opens on the world map. SaveLoadStatus Outcome of reading a save slot. UpgradeEffectKind What one authored permanent-upgrade effect does. reference/TDMaker.Unity.Hud.GameHud.html.title: Class GameHud | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.Hud.GameHud.html.summary: Class GameHud Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Hud Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Production HUD for PC (mouse + keyboard), built in uGUI from code and styled by a HudTheme: top bar (gold, lives, wave, pause, speed), wave-call indicators at path entrances (countdown ring, early bonus), radial build menu, tower panel (upgrades, branches, abilities, target priority, rally, sell), hero portraits, spell bar with cooldowns and hotkeys, unit info, pause and victory/defeat screens, tooltips and world feedback (range ellipses, slot highlight, placement ghost, rally/move markers, spell aim). Interaction follows the input grammar of spec 14 (docs/specs/14-input-grammar.md): one selection or aiming state at a time; a battlefield left click acts at the release point; while a hero, rally point or spell is being aimed every battlefield click is a point attempt (valid: act and return to browsing; invalid: feedback and keep aiming); build, upgrade, branch, ability, sell and wave call are single clicks; right click cancels everything (and does nothing without a selection); Esc cancels a selection, otherwise opens/closes the pause menu. Failed or cancelled aims send no command and every result shown is read back from the simulation. Keys: Esc cancel/pause, Space/P pause, 1-9 spells, H hero, N next wave, F1 debug overlay. Text is TextMesh Pro; every string comes from Texts (keys in HudTexts), and the HUD relabels itself when the language or a table changes. reference/TDMaker.Unity.Hud.html.title: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Hud | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.Hud.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.Hud Classes CachedNumber Caches the string for an integer so frequently updated labels do not allocate: the text of every value seen is kept (NumberText; with a prefix or suffix, per cache), so a value that comes back costs nothing. CachedText Caches the formatted text of a key with one integer (for example "Sell +{0}"), keeping the text of every number seen until the texts (Version: language, tables) change, so frequently updated labels do not allocate. ClickPicking Battlefield click-target rules used by GameHud (input grammar, spec 14 §1): every clickable thing has an axis-aligned world rectangle placed relative to its reference point; a click hits it only strictly inside (the border is excluded). Among the hits the higher selection priority wins, then the lower world reference point (smaller y). Equal priority and equal y keep the first candidate found. DamageNumbers Pooled floating damage and heal numbers (TextMesh Pro, outlined) on a screen-space canvas. Numbers are merged per target for a short window so rapid hits do not flood the screen; digits come from a cached string table and fading uses the canvas renderer alpha, so steady-state updates do not allocate. Toggle with damageNumbers. GameHud Production HUD for PC (mouse + keyboard), built in uGUI from code and styled by a HudTheme: top bar (gold, lives, wave, pause, speed), wave-call indicators at path entrances (countdown ring, early bonus), radial build menu, tower panel (upgrades, branches, abilities, target priority, rally, sell), hero portraits, spell bar with cooldowns and hotkeys, unit info, pause and victory/defeat screens, tooltips and world feedback (range ellipses, slot highlight, placement ghost, rally/move markers, spell aim). Interaction follows the input grammar of spec 14 (docs/specs/14-input-grammar.md): one selection or aiming state at a time; a battlefield left click acts at the release point; while a hero, rally point or spell is being aimed every battlefield click is a point attempt (valid: act and return to browsing; invalid: feedback and keep aiming); build, upgrade, branch, ability, sell and wave call are single clicks; right click cancels everything (and does nothing without a selection); Esc cancels a selection, otherwise opens/closes the pause menu. Failed or cancelled aims send no command and every result shown is read back from the simulation. Keys: Esc cancel/pause, Space/P pause, 1-9 spells, H hero, N next wave, F1 debug overlay. Text is TextMesh Pro; every string comes from Texts (keys in HudTexts), and the HUD relabels itself when the language or a table changes. HudButton A themed button built from code: background, optional icon, label, secondary label, cooldown shade and badge. Reports hover for tooltips and previews. Setters only touch components when a value changes. HudSprites Procedurally generated UI sprites used when a HudTheme slot is empty. All are white/grayscale so theme colours tint them. Panels and buttons are 9-sliced. HudTheme Look of the production HUD and of the world-space feedback (ranges, rally, aim). Every sprite slot is optional: empty slots use generated sprites from HudSprites. Create one with Assets/Create/2D Tower Defense Maker/HUD Theme and assign it to GameHud. HudTheme.IconOverride A HUD icon for one key. HudUi Small helpers that build themed uGUI elements from code. LanguageSelector Small native-language buttons for the sample title screens. Choices persist outside campaign slots. NumberText Shared strings for integers (0..TableSize-1 in a table, other values in a bounded map): each number is turned into a string once per session, so labels that show changing counts, timers or health do not allocate when a value comes back. Enums GameHud.Mode Interaction state. Spell aiming is tracked separately (AimingSpell) and always runs in Browsing.

reference/TDMaker.Unity.View.AudioCuePla.title: Class AudioCuePlayer | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.View.AudioCuePla.summary: Class AudioCuePlayer Namespace TDMaker.Unity.View Assembly TDMaker.Unity.dll Plays AudioCues through a small pool of AudioSources and routes global game events (waves, building, selling, victory ...) and mechanic events (chains, traps, mines, beams, heals, shields, reflection, knockback, companions, returning units, body raising) to cues. Per-template cues (attack, hit, death, projectiles, spells) are routed by EntityViewRegistry; the HUD plays the interface cues (click, build menu, rally, wave call). Every slot is optional. Volumes come from TDGameSettings (Master × SFX or UI) and each channel may route to an AudioMixerGroup. Each cue respects its minInterval, at most Max Voices Per Cue copies play at once and the pool never grows past Voices (the oldest voice is reused), so dense fights do not stack sounds or allocate. reference/TDMaker.Unity.View.html.title: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.View | 2D Tower Defense Maker API
reference/TDMaker.Unity.View.html.summary: Namespace TDMaker.Unity.View Classes ArtSet A swappable set of sprites keyed by view key (template view keys and projectile view keys). Assign one to an EntityViewRegistry to draw units, towers and projectiles with these sprites instead of the generated primitives; anything without an entry keeps its prefab or primitive look, so partial sets are fine. Swapping the asset swaps the whole look without code changes. Also carries the build plot sprite drawn by LevelView. Create one with Assets/Create/2D Tower Defense Maker/Art Set. ArtSet.Entry Sprites for one view key. AudioCuePlayer Plays AudioCues through a small pool of AudioSources and routes global game events (waves, building, selling, victory ...) and mechanic events (chains, traps, mines, beams, heals, shields, reflection, knockback, companions, returning units, body raising) to cues. Per-template cues (attack, hit, death, projectiles, spells) are routed by EntityViewRegistry; the HUD plays the interface cues (click, build menu, rally, wave call). Every slot is optional. Volumes come from TDGameSettings (Master × SFX or UI) and each channel may route to an AudioMixerGroup. Each cue respects its minInterval, at most Max Voices Per Cue copies play at once and the pool never grows past Voices (the oldest voice is reused), so dense fights do not stack sounds or allocate. AudioCuePlayer.GlobalCues Cues for global game events. AudioCuePlayer.KeyedCue A cue for one mechanic id (chain, trap, mine, beam, pulse, reflection, transfer or raise id), status effect id or template id (companions, returning units). AudioCuePlayer.MechanicCues Default cues for the built-in mechanic events. A AudioCuePlayer.KeyedCue with the mechanic's id overrides them. EllipseRenderer A smooth range ellipse: a filled mesh plus an outline line. Its shape always comes from RangeShape, the same ellipse the simulation uses for range checks, so what is drawn is what is hit. EntityView Pooled visual for one simulation entity: interpolated position, y-sorting, facing, optional health bar, hit flash, death fade, status-effect tint and icons, tower tier pips, projectile trail and orientation, hero death/return presentation, and an optional Animator driven with the standard parameters (Move bool, Speed float, Attack/Hit/Die triggers; missing parameters are skipped). Add it to custom prefabs to control sorting and the body renderer; it is added automatically otherwise. EntityView.AnimatorParameters Animator parameter names driven by the view. EntityViewRegistry Creates, pools and updates EntityViews from simulation events. Prefabs come from authoring assets or the TDMaker.Unity.View.EntityViewRegistry.overrides list (by view key); otherwise generated primitive sprites are used. Also routes per-template presentation hooks (VFX prefabs through VfxPool, audio cues through AudioCuePlayer) and draws built-in feedback: impact flashes, splash rings and instant-hit beams. EntityViewRegistry.ViewOverride Maps a view key to a prefab, overriding the asset's own prefab. LevelView Draws level geometry for samples and prototypes: a generated ground texture (grass, roads that follow the lanes, rocks, tufts and trees), path entry/exit markers and stone build pads. Everything is procedural and deterministic. MusicPlayer Plays background music: a menu loop while no battle is shown, the level's battle loop (music, falling back to this component's defaults), an optional intense loop from configurable waves (last wave, waves flagged bossWave, or from a wave number) and victory / defeat stingers that stop or duck the loop. Changes crossfade between two pooled AudioSources; a third plays stingers. Volume = track × TDGameSettings Music × Master, routed to the Music mixer group when one is set. No allocation per frame; every clip is optional (an empty slot is silent). PointerInput Mouse and keyboard access that works with both the Input System package and the legacy Input Manager. PrimitiveSprites Procedurally generated sprites (1 world unit across) so samples work with zero imported art. Every shape exists as a flat white silhouette and as an outlined, top-lit grayscale version; both are tinted by the renderer colour. Shapes are described by signed distance functions in unit space (-0.5..0.5, y up). SimProfilerMarkers Core profiling hook that wraps every fixed step and every pipeline stage (system) in a Unity Unity.Profiling.ProfilerMarker, so the Unity Profiler shows TDMaker.Sim.Step with one child marker per stage (TDMaker.Sim.Motion, TDMaker.Sim.Ranged, ...). Another ISimProfiler can be chained through Next; it receives every callback after the marker begins and before it ends. SimulationRunner Owns a Simulation and advances it with the core SimulationClock from Update (catch-up limit = catch-up ticks × speed per frame). Events produced during a frame are dispatched in emission order through EventRaised and then cleared, so the event buffer (Event Capacity) must hold every tick a frame catches up (at most catch-up ticks × speed). Commands queued after the game ended are rejected by the core with GameEnded on the next frame (the clock no longer steps, so the runner flushes them). TDCameraController Orthographic 2D camera for a level: frames the level on start using the level's CameraFramingData (fit the whole map, fit its height or width and scroll, or a fixed view size; start focus and optional intro pan) at any aspect ratio, and optionally pans (screen edge, middle-mouse drag, WASD/arrows, left drag from empty ground) and zooms (mouse wheel, +/-), always clamped to the bounds. Toggles live in TDGameSettings. TDGameSettings Player-facing presentation toggles read by the camera, HUD and feedback components. Put one in the scene (components find it automatically) and expose its fields in your options menu. TDHud Minimal IMGUI heads-up display for PC (mouse and keyboard): economy and wave status, wave calling, speed control, slot/tower menus (build, branching upgrades, abilities, target priority, sell, rally), hero portraits with level/XP/skills/respawn timer and click-to-move, and spell buttons with click-to-target. Every range, aim and pick ellipse uses RangeShape, the same shape as the simulation's range check. UpgradeRunRecord The permanent upgrades of one run: the shop's name, the purchased rank of every track and the forced rank (-1 = none). Saved next to a recorded command log (<file>.upgrades.json) so a replay rebuilds the same snapshot. VfxPool Pools VFX prefab instances. Particle systems on an instance are restarted on reuse and the instance returns to the pool after its lifetime (particle duration + start lifetime, or TDMaker.Unity.View.VfxPool.defaultLifetime). Interfaces IPooledVfx Implement on a VFX prefab's components to be told when a pooled instance is (re)used. Enums GroundStyle How LevelView draws the ground. MusicPlayer.State What the player is currently playing. MusicPlayer.StingerMode What a victory or defeat stinger does to the battle loop. TDKey Keyboard keys used by the default PC controls. Delegates SimEventHandler Receives simulation events without copying them. TemplateDecorator Changes a baked template before the simulation is created (for example to add WithCustomData values). asset is the authoring asset the template came from, or null. Return the template to use.
